haiku-low.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time runs on recovery. Older missed fire times are dropped silently with no history entry.
haiku-low.q2: It is recorded as a run with status skipped, finished_at set, and no attempts. It is not executed.
haiku-low.q3: Up to 3 attempts in total. Wait 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2. After attempt 3 the run ends as failed.
haiku-low.q4: After 2 minutes without a heartbeat, the reaper takes it over. Yes, that uses up an attempt, since attempts are counted at claim time.
haiku-low.q5: The executing run finishes normally. Pending and retry_wait runs are cancelled. On resume, next_fire_at is set to the first fire time after now, and nothing is caught up.
haiku-low.q6: UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING allows only one run. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the schedule row also limits who processes it.
haiku-low.q7: In job_schedules.next_fire_at. It changes when a run is created (set to the next fire time after now), on disable (set to NULL), and on re-enable or resume (recomputed).
haiku-low.q8: A claim query selects one claimable run with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. In the same transaction it sets status to running, increments attempt_count, and sets claimed_by.
haiku-low.q9: In job_runs.heartbeat_at, refreshed every 30 seconds by the running worker. The reaper notices runs with status running whose heartbeat is older than 2 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: The wait is stored in next_attempt_at on the job_runs row, set to now plus 1 or 5 minutes. The retry starts when the same claim query finds it due.
haiku-low.q11: Once per fire time: a job_runs row, unique on schedule_id and fire_time. Once per execution try: a job_attempts row, unique on run_id and attempt_no.
haiku-low.q12: Every outcome write requires status running and attempt_count matching its fencing token. If 0 rows change, the stale worker does nothing and its result is discarded.

sonnet.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time runs (as a late run). Older missed ones are dropped with no history entry. (If an old run is still running or in retry_wait, the reaper first handles a stale running one; a retry_wait old run would make the new fire time skipped.)
sonnet.q2: It is recorded as a run with status `skipped` (finished_at = now(), no attempts) and not executed.
sonnet.q3: At most 3 attempts. Wait is 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2 (run is retry_wait in between). If attempt 3 fails, the run ends as `failed` with finished_at set.
sonnet.q4: After the heartbeat is stale for 2 minutes, the reaper abandons the attempt and sets the run to retry_wait with 1 or 5 minute backoff counted from detection, after which any worker can claim it. Yes, the attempt was counted at claim time, so it uses one of the 3; if it was attempt 3 the run becomes failed.
sonnet.q5: The executing run is left alone and finishes normally; if it fails, its retry is cancelled by the cancel statement (failed attempt stays in history). The waiting (pending/retry_wait) run is set to cancelled. On resume, next_fire_at is recomputed as the first fire time after now(), so fire times during the pause are not caught up.
sonnet.q6: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the schedule row means only one worker gets it, and UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING allows only one run per fire time.
sonnet.q7: In job_schedules.next_fire_at (null when disabled). It is set to the first fire time after now() when a run is created for the schedule, set to NULL on disable, and recomputed on re-enable/resume.
sonnet.q8: A claim query selects a claimable run with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1 and, in the same statement, updates it to running with attempt_count+1, claimed_by and heartbeat_at; the row lock means only one worker gets it.
sonnet.q9: In job_runs.heartbeat_at (refreshed every 30 seconds by the running worker). The reaper step of every worker's loop notices when it is older than 2 minutes for a running run.
sonnet.q10: In job_runs: status retry_wait with next_attempt_at = now() + backoff. When next_attempt_at <= now(), the normal claim query picks it up like any other run and starts the next attempt.
sonnet.q11: Once per fire time: a job_runs row (unique on schedule_id, fire_time). Once per execution try: a job_attempts row (unique on run_id, attempt_no).
sonnet.q12: Its outcome write is conditioned on the fencing token (WHERE id=$run AND status='running' AND attempt_count=$my_attempt). After takeover the attempt_count/status no longer match, so 0 rows are affected and the worker does nothing more; its result is discarded.
